headline: Highest risk is medium: Superset can egress to allowlisted APIs while the paired awesome-python collection has no runtime safeguards, creating modest but real leakage and workflow-conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default instruction-bridging channel is documented. agent_a is a non-runnable collection with no io_surfaces, and agent_b only exposes calls_apis to the Superset API; neither profile shows shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP ingestion that would let one agent inject instructions into the other.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies agent_a content into agent_b prompts without sanitization, injection risk appears.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added between the pair, the severity increases.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared prompt channels.
Do not paste agent_a content into agent_b prompts.
Add provenance labels to any copied text.
requires-engineering: add content sanitization before any cross-agent handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and has network_egress none, while agent_b has allowlisted egress and calls_apis. With no shared workspace or secrets listed, leakage is not evidenced, but if either agent is fed sensitive files, agent_b could transmit them through its API surface.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed into a shared workspace consumed by agent_b, leakage risk becomes material.
IF agent_b is configured to send file contents through its API calls, data exposure increases.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared directory.
Restrict agent_b API calls to non-sensitive datasets.
Review outbound allowlist entries before use.
requires-engineering: add per-file redaction before API submission.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles show no overlapping write surfaces, locks, or shared mutable resources. agent_a is non-runnable and has no io_surfaces; agent_b only lists API calls. That makes direct write conflict unlikely, though uncertainty remains because the orchestrator and any hidden workspace are undocumented.
conditions: IF both agents are later given write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict risk rises.
IF an orchestrator introduces shared mutable state without locking, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only by default.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b can act on API-backed data engineering workflows, while agent_a is a curated collection that could be treated as authoritative reference material. If agent_b consumes agent_a-derived content without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions; the pair lacks any documented validation step.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a content as authoritative input, cascading errors become likely.
IF downstream actions are triggered from unverified summaries, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on cross-agent outputs.
Add a verification step in agent_b workflows.
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation on handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for either agent. agent_a touches no data classes and agent_b lists no secrets handled or regulated data, so a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced in this pair.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is later introduced into either agent, reassess compliance.
IF residency or retention policies are added and differ, compliance risk may emerge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
